He Bought a New Chevy Corvette in April 2026 and He Wants It Gone After Less Than 700 Miles
14 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
There are countless Chevrolet Corvette blue-collar supercars looking for new homes on the used car market at any given moment in most parts of the world, and even more in the States, and this C8 Stingray is just one of them.
So, what caught our attention that made us dedicate an entire story to it? The fact that it is brand new, yet its owner wants it gone. What is the reason, you ask? Well, that’s a very good question, though we do not know the answer. If you do, feel free to drop a line below. What we can tell you is that the man bought it in April 2026, adding less than 700 miles (1,125 km) since.
In fact, the digital odometer revealed 686 miles (1,104 km) at the time of cataloging, and that translates to a little over 100 miles (160 km) per month on average since the car left the dealership. The seller paid $83,965 for this 2026 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray , which is a Coupe 2LT in case you were wondering, and now he wants it gone, hence why he listed it for sale as part of an ongoing auction on Cars&Bids.
Before moving on to the details, we will tell you that a used C8 Chevy Corvette normally sells for $50,000 to $90,000 in today’s used car market. We have seen some examples that broke into the $40,000 zone, and those were earlier model years. Later model years tend to fetch over $80,000, and it is not uncommon to see some change hands for more than $90,000. Thus, it all comes down to the model year, mileage, and specification, and you should keep in mind that convertibles are a bit more expensive than coupes.
Photo: Cars&Bids On average, the 2026 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray Coupe 2LT fetches between $75,000 and $86,000, and it will be interesting to see how much this example gets when the gavel hits the table six days from now, on October 20, 2026. Since we have told you about the Benjamins, we should also tell you that the highest bid at the time of writing was $10,100, and there is obviously a reserve on it that clearly hasn’t been met.
Finished in Blade Silver Metallic, this Chevrolet Corvette Stingray has a Sky Cool Gray interior. It features 19-inch wheels at the front and 20-inch wheels at the rear, has a removable roof panel, heated and ventilated seats, yellow seatbelts, leather upholstery, a head-up display, a Bose sound system, and a performance data and video recorder for extra fun at the local racetrack, the listing reveals.
This ‘Vette does not feature the newer motor, which is a small-black 6.7-liter V8. The LS6 is officially good for 535 hp (453 ps/399 kW ) and 520 lb-ft (705 Nm) of torque in the 2027 Chevrolet Corvette Stingray . With the optional Z51 Performance Pack, the car hits 60 mph (97 kph) in just 2.8 seconds, though some tests have revealed that it is a bit faster than that. It completes the standing quarter mile in 11 seconds at 124 mph (200 kph), and taps out at over 200 mph (322+ kph).
Photo: Cars&Bids Powering the pictured Corvette is the old 6.2-liter V8, which is rated at 490 horsepower (497 ps/365 kW). Thus, the car does not feature the Performance Exhaust System or the Z51 Performance Package, as if it did, then it would have had 495 hp (502 ps/369 kW). The output is channeled to the rear wheels through an eight-speed automatic transmission. This model hit 60 mph (97 kph) in as little as 2.9 seconds, and ran the quarter mile in over 11 seconds from a standstill.
Due to the extremely low mileage, this Chevrolet Corvette Stingray has not required servicing, and there is nothing wrong with it, as the car is in top-notch condition. Besides the vehicle, is offered with a clean Carfax history report, and has a clean Florida title, the next owner will also get two keys, the window sticker, and the owner’s manual. The seller noted that the tires carry 2026 and 2025 date code tires, and that’s nothing to be worried about, obviously, as the only thing this ride needs is gasoline in the tank a petrolhead behind the wheel.
We are curious to find out how much this rear mid-engined, rear-wheel drive blue-collar supercar will fetch once the gavel hits the table on the ongoing online auction, so we will keep an eye on the listing. And if you want to spruce up your life with the pictured Corvette, then you should check it out in more detail here on the quoted website. That is also where you can bid on it.
But realistically speaking, how much would you pay for this machine, knowing that you could get a brand-new ‘Vette with the new motor from $71,300 (MSRP)?
